title: 约客
author: 赵师秀
intro: A rainy summer night, frogs croaking everywhere, and a friend who promised to come still hasn’t shown up. The poet sits alone, tapping chess pieces — and we feel his waiting without being told.
analysis: 这首诗写一个雨夜等朋友的小场景。“黄梅时节”是江南初夏的梅雨季，天天下雨，所以“家家雨”；池塘边青草茂盛，到处都是青蛙在叫，所以“处处蛙”。前两句写外面热闹的雨声、蛙声，正好反衬屋里的安静。第三句点题：约好的客人没来，已经过了半夜。最后一句最妙：诗人没说自己着急、失望，只写他一个人无聊地敲着棋子，把灯芯烧结成的“灯花”都震落了。一个小动作，写出等了很久、有点焦急又有点无奈的心情。这种不直接说感情、用动作和景物来表达的方法，叫“借景抒情”“以动写情”。
analysisEn: This short poem captures a small moment: waiting on a rainy night for a friend who doesn’t come. The “plum-yellow season” is early summer south of the Yangtze, when it rains day after day — so “rain on every house”. The ponds are thick with grass and full of croaking frogs. These first two lines are noisy with rain and frogs, and that noise makes the quiet inside the room feel even quieter. The third line tells us the situation: a guest promised to come, and now it is past midnight. The last line is the famous one. The poet never says he is impatient or disappointed. He just sits there idly tapping a chess piece on the board — tapping so long that the burnt “flower” on the lamp wick falls off. One small gesture shows how long he has waited and how he feels: a little restless, a little resigned. Letting an action carry the emotion, instead of naming it, is something Chinese poets love to do.
background: Zhao Shixiu (1170–1219) was a Southern Song poet from Yongjia (today’s Wenzhou, Zhejiang), one of the “Four Spirits of Yongjia” who wrote in a plain, finely observed style. This quatrain is his best-known poem.
pronunciation: 过夜半：过 guò。灯花：灯芯燃烧后结成的花状小块，不是真的花。
version: 采用通行教材版本。“青草池塘”有的本子作“青草池边”，“有约不来”有本作“约客不来”，网站不用。

lines.py: huáng méi shí jié jiā jiā yǔ
lines.lit: In the yellow-plum season, rain on every house;
lines.en: Plum-rain season: rain on every roof,

lines.py: qīng cǎo chí táng chù chù wā
lines.en: frogs croaking in every grassy pond.

lines.py: yǒu yuē bù lái guò yè bàn
lines.lit: There was an appointment, he hasn’t come, past midnight;
lines.en: He promised to come — midnight has passed;

lines.py: xián qiāo qí zǐ luò dēng huā
lines.lit: idly I tap chess pieces, knocking down the lamp-wick flower.
lines.en: idly I tap a chess piece, and the lamp’s charred wick drops away.

words.note: 约：约定、邀请。现代汉语“约朋友”“有约”仍这样用。

words.en: the season when plums turn yellow (early summer)
words.note: 江南五六月梅子黄熟，雨多，今天叫“梅雨季节”“黄梅天”。
叠字表示“每一”，现代汉语说“家家户户”。
现代汉语仍用，也说“到处”。
现代汉语说“过了半夜”“半夜以后”。
现代汉语仍用，口语读 qízi。

words.en: the charred, flower-shaped tip of a burning wick
words.note: 古代油灯的灯芯烧久了结成小花一样的炭块；今天用电灯，已经见不到了。

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: 连绵的梅雨既是客人不来的原因，也把夜晚衬得更寂寞。
imagery.en: The endless early-summer rain may be why the friend doesn’t come — and it makes the night feel lonelier.

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 池塘边青草茂盛、蛙声一片，写出江南初夏的生机，反衬屋里的冷清。
imagery.en: Lush grass and croaking frogs show a lively early summer outside, in contrast to the quiet room.

imagery.name: 灯
imagery.zh: 灯花一点点结起又落下，暗示等得太久，只有一盏灯陪着诗人。
imagery.en: The wick burns down until its charred tip falls: he has waited a long time, with only the lamp for company.
